loop.top3_series_pattern: seasonal_dominated with strong 52‑week cycle and moderate predictability; model rankings unstable across windows and several models share correlated errors
loop.top3_why: The mean of the full pool (strategy A) offers the most stable performance across the three validation windows (0.65, 0.733, 0.717) and is robust to the unstable ranking and correlated errors highlighted in the diagnosis. Although the DBA strategy (C) has a slightly lower overall score, its per‑window performance is highly variable (0.744, 0.589, 0.864), indicating sensitivity to the particular window and potential overfitting to the limited validation data. The weighted strategy (B) shows even more variability and a higher gap to the best score. Therefore, the plain mean provides the safest generalization to the blind test window.
loop.top3_why_not: Strategy B’s weights, derived from a meta‑model trained on other series, introduce high variance in a setting with only three validation windows and unstable model rankings, leading to inconsistent performance. Strategy C’s DBA, while theoretically powerful, exhibits extreme window‑to‑window swings, suggesting it may overfit to the specific validation splits and not generalize well to unseen data.
